title: Reply to @roninjoey #thelightinthepiazza #musicals #broadway
transcript: So “The Light in the Piazza” Am I overthinking it? If I have to ask I probably am... but here are my thoughts: They're not wholly original — people have been talking about this show and its problems for a long time Let me break it down a little bit I’ve written down my thoughts - apologies if it looks like I'm reading cuz I am on one hand you have a show featuring a neurodivergent individual as a result of a traumatic brain injury: Clara But everyone around her is afraid to talk about it especially to Clara. On the other hand the musical is based on a novella that was written when such terms didn't even exist and it was pretty revolutionary to showcase someone with a disability as someone who could be loved. On the other hand the musical is presented to contemporary audiences as a “love conquers all” narrative which dimensions the support and research that's gone into overcoming decades of mismanagement and misunderstanding of their needs. On the other hand the musical to me is more than just a love story It's also a tragedy — It's both things. The ending is unresolved and we are not sure what will happen to margaret and clara Their growth is just beginning. Their storylines will face the ultimate challenge following the curtain call especially for Margaret. But messy storylines make for great theater, right? And then ... On the other hand the musical is written through the lens of Margaret. It's her story. We barely get to know who Clara is and what she thinks beyond a few oblique solos and duets where she's responding to the world around her and people are singing to her. We don't get to know what she thinks and feels really. Her narrative doesn't exist. She's a plot point in many ways. On the other hand — the music is so pretty! What do you think?
